findings.title: Team admins and owners are incorrectly denied permission to add guests
findings.body: The team permission check combines `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`. A membership normally has one of these roles, so a team admin who is not the booking's assigned organizer (and an owner if the helpers are role-specific) fails this check even though the UI explicitly exposes this action to `isUserTeamAdminOrOwner`. Use `||` (or the project’s established combined-role authorization helper) so either privileged team role is accepted.

findings.title: The API permits duplicate guest emails in a single request
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` only filters out attendees that existed before this mutation; it never deduplicates `guests` itself. Although the dialog validates duplicates, callers can invoke the tRPC endpoint directly because the server schema has no uniqueness refinement. A request such as `["guest@example.com", "guest@example.com"]` therefore attempts to create duplicate attendee records (or fails the entire operation if a database uniqueness constraint exists), and can produce duplicate calendar/email effects. Deduplicate and normalize the input server-side, or reject duplicate input before `createMany`.

findings.title: Attendee-initiated updates use the attendee's calendar credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: The handler explicitly authorizes any existing attendee at line 52, but obtains credentials from `ctx.user` here. For an attendee adding a guest, these are the attendee's integrations, not the booking organizer's destination-calendar credentials. `updateCalendarAttendees` will consequently be unable to update the organizer's calendar (or may target an inappropriate connected calendar), after the attendee rows have already been inserted. Resolve credentials for the booking owner/calendar connection when updating the booking's calendar.

findings.title: A calendar-update failure leaves permanently inconsistent booking state
findings.body: The new attendees are committed to the database at lines 92-106 before the external calendar update is attempted here. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation returns an error but the database still contains the guests; retrying then filters those emails as already present and rejects the request, so the caller cannot repair the missing calendar invitation/update through this feature. Add compensation/retry handling or structure the operation so failed external synchronization is recorded and can be retried rather than treating the database write as a completed update.

findings.title: Existing addresses in a mixed request receive a new-booking email
findings.body: The email sender is passed the original `guests` array rather than `uniqueGuests`. If a request contains one already-attending email plus one genuinely new email, `sendAddGuestsEmails` classifies the existing attendee as a newly added guest and sends it `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a booking confirmation) even though no attendee was added for that address. Pass the filtered list of actually-created emails to ensure only new invitees receive the scheduled email.
